notes.finding: Two theoretical spy blind spots, confirmed empirically on this host (py 3.12.13): (a) pathlib file reads (read_text/read_bytes -> io.open) are NOT counted -- io.open is the same function object as builtins.open but a distinct module attribute, so patching builtins.open leaves pathlib reads invisible (probe: counts stayed {} for Path.read_text); (b) os.scandir/os.listdir and C-level opens (np.load) are unspied. Not blocking: every op class the OLD per-call path performed (native_lw.py:49-115: mkdir, dylib/stamp exists, stamp read_text+json.loads, kernel read_bytes, sha256, CDLL, which, subprocess) still has at least one spied chokepoint (Path.exists/is_file and os.path.exists route through os.stat at call time on 3.12 -- probe counted 3/3; the kernel read exists only to be hashed -> hashlib.sha256; the stamp read only to be json.loads-ed). Independently, the structural read of execute() (native_handle.py:412-518) and of every helper it calls (lw_native.py:102-160) contains no IO of any kind, and entries/argtypes are bound eagerly at prepare (native_handle.py:538-546), so there is no lazy init left to fire inside execute() on any input class.

The pairwise-distinct taxonomy assertion uses `a is not b` (object identity), which would not catch one class being a SUBCLASS of another. The property itself holds -- all five are direct sibling subclasses of NativeHandleError (native_handle.py:114-144) and `not issubclass(a, UnsupportedInput)` is asserted -- but the assertion is weaker than its comment suggests.
notes.repair_if_touched: Assert `not (issubclass(a, b) or issubclass(b, a))` for each pair.

notes.finding: The in-lock double-check consults only _REGISTRY, not _NEG_CACHE. Two same-key threads that both pass the fast path before a failure is cached will each re-run full artifact validation (redundant IO, ~ms scale; steady-state caching is separately proven by test_missing_artifact_never_builds_and_is_cached:445-448, retry does zero IO). No correctness impact.
notes.repair_if_touched: Also re-read _NEG_CACHE.get(key) in the double-check and raise it.

notes.finding: Real-fork coverage and multi-threaded fork: the reviewer additionally ran a REAL os.fork probe (beyond the author's pid-injection test): the child raised StaleNativeHandle on the parent handle, re-prepared a distinct handle under its own pid, and reproduced the parent's output bitwise -- the pid guard genuinely re-prepares in a forked child. Remaining edges are out of N8-10 scope but must be carried: (a) a fork WHILE another thread holds _REGISTRY_LOCK/_dir_lock could deadlock the child (inherent to lock-based modules; ARCHITECTURE permits 'only spawn-based execution is supported and tested'; fork-vs-spawn policy belongs to the pool owner N8-14); (b) _REGISTRY grows one entry per (pid, generation, dir, ...) key -- negligible per workflow, but a long-lived process bumping new_workflow_generation per tile accumulates handles/CDLLs (retention is intentional per the no-dlclose rule).
notes.repair_if_touched: N8-14 integration: state the fork policy explicitly; consider bounding registry size per pid.

notes.finding: A present manifest.json whose 'files' is absent or non-dict passes silently (comment defers full schema validation to N8-21), and member paths are joined as artifact_dir / rel WITHOUT containment checks -- a manifest entry like '../x' or a special file would be hashed (potentially unbounded read, e.g. a FIFO); members are only ever hashed, never executed, so this is a robustness edge, not a code-execution vector. ARCHITECTURE requires 'path containment and no symlink escape' for the packaged loader.
notes.repair_if_touched: N8-21: reject non-dict files, and require rel paths that resolve inside artifact_dir with no symlink escape before hashing.

evidence: Spy scope is correct: IoSpy is armed ONLY around the execute loop (test:163-176) and around identity() (test:190-192); prepare happens before arming, so warm-path proof is not diluted by expected prepare IO. Strongest form: there is NO warmup execute before arming -- the first f64 call, first f32 call, first caller-out call and every first bundle-shape all occur under the armed spy (150 executes; entry counters match the tally exactly: test:176-177).

Old-path op-class coverage: the per-call path (native_lw.py:49-115 via native_longwave_primary:130 -> _ensure_loaded) performs mkdir, dylib.exists, stamp.exists, stamp.read_text+json.loads, kernel.read_bytes, sha256, and on a build ispc-which+subprocess -- each has at least one spied chokepoint (os.mkdir/makedirs/stat/lstat; json.loads/load; hashlib.sha256; subprocess.run/Popen; ctypes.CDLL; shutil.which). os.stat chokepoint empirically intercepts Path.exists/is_file and os.path.exists on py3.12. Blind spots (io.open via pathlib, scandir, C-level opens) documented as note N1 -- structurally irrelevant because execute() contains no IO.

Lazy-init audit: execute() (native_handle.py:412-518) resolves _getpid at call time, then calls only the pure lw_native validation helpers (_need_array/_need_c_contig/_scalar_spec/_reflection_spec/_buffer/_extent/_ranges_overlap -- numpy introspection and pointer arithmetic only, lw_native.py:102-160), np.zeros/np.empty/view, and the pre-bound entry pointer. Both f32/f64 entries AND their argtypes/restype are set eagerly at prepare (native_handle.py:538-547), so no ctypes/dlopen init can fire lazily on first call, first spec, or first caller-out. B=0 returns np.zeros((0,7)) before touching any pointer (native_handle.py:436-438; no-C-entry proven at test:180-185; np.zeros does no filesystem IO).

Sanctioned non-input divergences, none touching input rejection: post-launch exceptions wrapped NativeExecutionError (native_handle.py:513-517; contract n8_04_typed_lw_contract.md sec.3 'post-launch failures propagate' -- loud RuntimeError, never caught by _dispatch, proven at test:244-257); pid checked first -> StaleNativeHandle (422-426); gang/ISA validated at prepare -> UnsupportedNativeISA instead of the shipped per-call UnsupportedInput/FileNotFoundError for gang misuse or missing dylib (capability/configuration failure, outside the 17-arg input domain, per ARCHITECTURE capability-vs-input separation).

Five sibling subclasses of NativeHandleError(RuntimeError): MissingNativeArtifact, CorruptNativeArtifact, UnsupportedNativeISA, NativeExecutionError, StaleNativeHandle (native_handle.py:114-144). None is or subclasses UnsupportedInput (TypeError); asserted at test:420-427 (see note N2 on assertion strength).

Auto-decline vs expert-loud wording separation exists as required: MissingNativeArtifact carries 'auto: the planner declines native pre-launch and keeps Numba. expert: build it explicitly with expert_build(...)' (native_handle.py:260-264, asserted at test:377); CorruptNativeArtifact stamp mismatch carries 'auto: decline native. expert: rebuild' (native_handle.py:298-301). ISA messages state the qualified domain without auto/expert routing (capability failure) -- consistent.

Missing artifact never builds: the prepare path calls only _validate_artifact + _load_entries; the only subprocess in the module is inside expert_build, which no prepare path references (verified by reading prepare_native_handle, native_handle.py:550-592). Proven at test:439-443 (zero subprocess.run/Popen on the miss) and the cached failure does zero IO on retry (test:445-448).

PID guard re-prepares in the child: execute resolves the module-global _getpid at call time (native_handle.py:422; test injects via nh._getpid, native_handle re-reads it -- sound). Beyond the author's simulation the reviewer ran a REAL os.fork probe: child raised StaleNativeHandle on the parent handle, prepare_native_handle in the child loaded a FRESH CDLL under the child's pid (registry key includes pid, native_handle.py:525-529), and output matched the parent bitwise. Parent handle kept working after the child exited.

Generation semantics per ARCHITECTURE: new_workflow_generation mints a token and clears _NEG_CACHE (native_handle.py:181-189) so new workflows retry unavailable capability; a RUNNING workflow keeps its already-issued handle (h1 still executes after the bump, test:313-323; the library stays resident). Negative cache is per (pid, generation, key) and cannot shadow a different dir (test:457-464); a new generation re-attempts IO (test:450-454).

Double-checked locking is closed deterministically, not by luck: same-key prepares serialize on the per-artifact-directory lock (_dir_lock, native_handle.py:170-178); the winner validates, loads and publishes under _REGISTRY_LOCK INSIDE the dir lock (590-591); the loser's recheck (576-579) happens after it acquires the dir lock, hence necessarily after publication -- exactly one CDLL and one shared handle object under any schedule. The 20ms-slowed _sha256_file (test:269-276) widens the validation window so 8 threads genuinely contend rather than finishing sequentially; correctness itself rests on lock ordering, not timing. expert_build publishes under the same per-dir lock with atomic renames and stamp LAST (642-670), so a concurrent reader sees old-complete or new-complete state.

No dlclose anywhere in the module; the CDLL owner is held in the handle slot and the registry never evicts -- 'retaining a loaded library until process exit' as the dossier requires (test_prepare_does_not_mutate_lw_native_globals additionally pins that lw_native._LIBS/_LIB_DIR are never touched; grep confirms zero assignments to lw_native attributes).
